To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mean age at diagnosis of TP53 mutation carriers with childhood adrenocorticoid sarcoma, rha-domyosarcoma and osteosarcoma is significantly lower than in the general population and that the mean age of TP53 mutation carrier with childhood brain tumours is also significantly lower but not so clearly separated.

the mean age at the diagnosis of childhood adrenocorticocellular sarcoma, rhibdomyosarcomas, osteosarcomas and brain tumours is significantly lower in families with germline p53 mutations than in the Czech population.
the mean age at cancer diagnosis of TP53 mutation carriers differs from the Czech population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of age at cancer diagnosis in families with TP53 germlin mutations and in the Czech general population.

the identification of TP53 germlines mutations in patients and their families with a high risk of developing malignancies, and with the analysis of the clinical and molecular characteristics of the tumours in these patients.
the identification of germline TP 53 mutations in the families of oncology and gynaecology patients, with the aim of providing the best possible treatment for these patients and their families.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in families of patients diagnosed with adrenocorticoal tumours or brain tumours before the age of 30 years or with rhabdomyo- or osteosarcomas before the age of ten years, TP53 mutation testing is indicated.
the TP53 mutation screening is useful in families of patients with the following tumours: adrenocorticoal carcinoma, rhabdmyosarcoma, breast carcinoma, brain tumour and osteosarcoma.
the identification of TP53 mutation is important in families of childhood adrenocortic sarcoma, rhapsarcoma, brain and osteosarcoma patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in families of oncological patients with a high incidence of early onset tumours (particularly brain tumour, adrenocortico-sarcoma, rhabdomi-osarcoma and osteosarcoma), it is important to search for TP53 mutations.
TP53 germlines mutations are not common in families of oncological patients.

TP53 mutation analysis is a valuable diagnostic test in the families of children with adrenocortial carcinoma, rhabdoid tumour or rhabdomyoblastoma and in families with two or more members affected by osteosarcoma or brain tumour.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in families with a history of childhood cancers, particularly adrenocortial sarcoma, rhatdomyosarcomas and osteosarcomas, TP53 gene mutation analysis is indicated.
the TP53 gene should be analysed in all families with two or more cases of childhood adrenocortex carcinoma, rhabdodyosarcoma, or osteosarcoma.
in families where a patient is diagnosed with one of these tumour types, the search for a TP53 mutation should be recommended.
